competitor_patterns: Extreme depth wins: OutdoorGearLab ranks #1 with 16,540 words and Bikerumor with 24,938 words — both 3-6x longer than our top posts; they combine lab-style scoring rubrics, per-model deep dives, and explicit methodology sections that justify their authority

Comparison tables are non-negotiable for top positions: every competitor in position 1-3 uses structured comparison tables with scored metrics (lens quality, fit, coverage, frame, field performance) — not just spec lists but rated scores per model

FAQ schema + real-world testing language drives AI Overview inclusion: top competitors use phrases like 'we tested 18 pairs', 'judged on real rides', 'five key metrics' — this signals to Google and AI engines that the content is empirically grounded, not just editorial

Category segmentation into sub-intents captures more SERP real estate: OutdoorGearLab's H2 structure (MTB, Road, Value, Budget Performance) allows one page to rank for multiple long-tail variants simultaneously — a hub-and-spoke within a single article

Recency signals are explicit and front-loaded: all top competitors include the year (2026) in H1, meta title, and publication/update date in the snippet — OutdoorGearLab's Jan 5 2026 date and Cyclist's Jul 27 2026 update show Google that freshness is actively maintained
our_gaps: Word count ceiling at ~8,000 words: our longest post is 8,098 words but top competitors average 16,000-25,000 words; we lack the per-model deep-dive sections (individual H2 per glass model with scored criteria) that make competitor pages authoritative hubs

No explicit scoring methodology or rubric: competitors use quantified scoring (e.g. '8.4/10 for lens quality') with transparent test criteria — our posts describe features but don't score models numerically, weakening E-E-A-T signals for AI and Google Quality Raters

10 posts are stub-length (1,057–1,310 words) with no FAQ schema and no comparison table: these pages dilute site quality signals and miss the structural minimum Google expects for competitive informational queries — especially the 11 stub posts flagged with faq_schema=NO

Missing sub-intent segmentation within pillar posts: we don't have dedicated sections for MTB vs Road vs Gravel vs Budget within our best-of posts, meaning we capture only the head query and miss long-tail variants that competitors dominate with the same URL

Thin internal linking architecture: with 40+ posts covering overlapping topics, we lack a clear hub page that consolidates authority — competitors use one mega-guide as the canonical hub and link satellites from it, concentrating PageRank instead of diluting it
